text:
olivia: quick check — i sketched an experimental 'regional band' approach for routing penalties. idea: compute cost and latency bands per region, then apply a small, bounded penalty that nudges routing without hard fails. thoughts?

sam: short version — sounds promising. avoids flip-flopping on noisy signals. how do you define bands? static thresholds or percentile-based?

olivia: percentile-based per-region (p50/p95) for latency, and normalized cost-per-token for cost. bands are like buckets: green/yellow/red with penalty weights [0, 0.1, 0.3] that apply to score.

maya: curious about edge cases — what if a region has low cost but very high p95 for specific models during burst? the band could mask hotspot.

jun: we can combine with a short-term probe signal: if p95 > band's threshold AND probe_fail_rate > 1% then escalate to hard fallback. band penalties are advisory only.

liam: can we see a config excerpt? easier to reason with concrete yaml/snippet.

olivia: sure, here's the prototype we used in the sim: 
```yaml
routing_policy:
  regional_bands:
    - region: us-west-2
      latency: {p50_ms: 20, p95_ms: 120}
      cost_per_token: 0.0008
      band_thresholds: {green: {p95: 100}, yellow: {p95: 160}, red: {p95: 300}}
      penalties: {green: 0.0, yellow: 0.08, red: 0.28}
  combine_strategy: weighted_sum # score + penalty*alpha
  hard_escalation: {probe_fail_rate_pct: 1.0, duration_sec: 30}
```

sam: ok, combine_strategy matters — weighted_sum alpha needs tuning. too high = effectively region lockout. too low = useless. we should also let tenant overrides set alpha=0 for performance-critical customers.

maya: metrics to watch in canary: per-region p50/p95, cost_per_request, routing_fraction, fallback_rate, and model_quality regressions. add a rolling-variance gauge to detect noisy bands.

jun: agree. propose rollout plan: 1) sim against historical traces 2) shadow traffic with penalized scoring (no effect) 3) 5% canary with traffic steering 4) full launch. each step gated on runbook signals.

liam: about policy engine impl — do we compute band penalties inside the policy-eval layer or as a post-score sink? my preference: inside eval so adapters can see the adjusted decision and explainability hooks remain consistent.

olivia: i'm leaning inside eval too so explainability/telemetry maps directly to final decision. downside: increased eval complexity and slightly higher latency per eval.

sam: latency hit probably negligible compared to network + model time if we keep band calc O(1). ensure we cache region stats and only recompute when rollup window advances.

maya: eviction/caching semantics: region stats should TTL ~30s with jitter. if stale, fall back to global default band. documentable fallback path is important.

jun: simulation notes — i ran 24h trace with alpha=0.2 and penalties as in olivia's snippet: routing fraction smoothed, cost delta -6% overall, p95 increased 2ms on avg in some tenants. no quality regressions.

liam: nice. we should add a kill-switch toggle that removes band penalties entirely per-tenant and globally. also an emergency route that pins to region with SLA.

olivia: agreed on kill-switch. i'll add policy flags: tenant_band_enabled, global_band_enabled, band_alpha_override.

infra-bot: deploy-check: policy-sim job completed for 4912345678 at 2025-03-06T18:14:02Z — 0 failures, 1 warning (variance high in eu-west-1).

sam: next actions: olivia will draft RFC patch for policy spec + eval impl details; jun will prepare sim config and canary playbook; maya will list telemetry dashboards and alert thresholds; liam will design caching/ttl and kill-switch plumbing.

olivia: i'll drop the RFC by EOD today. thanks all :thumbsup:
